title: land fast-forwards an orchestrator checkout that holds only unpushed item-file commits by rebasing them onto origin/main
goal: Retrospective of SP-avwlotax: the orchestrator committed an item-file edit (links on ST-q5r6e3nu) between landings; the next land (ST-jv27pfin) pushed and then left orch/s-avwlotax 5 commits behind origin/main ('Not possible to fast-forward'), so the orchestrator rebased and pushed by hand before the next claim. land rebases a clean checkout whose only commits beyond origin/main change item files onto origin/main after its push (or names the one command to run), so the next claim starts from the pushed main; and before its push land names the checkout's unpushed commits, its push carrying only the item's branch, never the checkout's whole local history.

gates.question: After its push, does land rebase a clean orchestrator checkout whose commits beyond origin/main change only item files, or only name the command?
options: rebase: land rebases those commits onto origin/main and says so, and names the command when any commit changes another file or the tree is dirty
name: land never rewrites the checkout and prints the one git rebase command in every case
gates.recommendation: rebase: land rebases those commits onto origin/main and says so, and names the command when any commit changes another file or the tree is dirty
gates.answer: rebase: land rebases those commits onto origin/main and says so, and names the command when any commit changes another file or the tree is dirty

gates.question: How many of the checkout's unpushed commits does land list by name before its push?

notes: Premise: fast_forward_start leaves a checkout that holds an unpushed commit behind origin/main (planned 2026-10-12: on a throwaway clone with one unpushed empty commit and one commit landed elsewhere it said 'land: left main 1 commit(s) behind origin/main: it cannot fast-forward' and rev-list HEAD..origin/main read 1). Merged ST-vybjfqvj (second-project run, bl_land.py fast_forward_start): same fault; absorbed: name the divergence before the push, and never push the whole local HEAD history. The suite sits at max_ids 100: extend TestLandedItem's test in test_land_e2e.py (it already covers the fast-forward) and rename it to carry the names the checks select, no new id. Gate behind-main answered: rebase (a local rebase, nothing pushed by it). Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 15 of 19, "Land snags: session-end distill, a stopped land's worktree, an orchestrator behind main and a racy hook test"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
